item.title: Dollar’s Reliance on Equity Inflows Seen Weighing on Currency
item.description: The dollar’s increasing dependence on equity inflows could erode the diversification benefit of leaving US assets unhedged, according to Deutsche Bank AG strategists, potentially putting downward pressure on the currency over time.

item.title: Petrobras Earnings Disappoint Despite Oil, Refining Tailwinds
item.description: Brazil’s state-controlled oil producer earnings missed estimates in the third-quarter despite record oil and gas production and a favorable backdrop of high crude prices and strong refining margins.

item.title: Macquarie to Pay Fine on Marketing Failure as New CEO Arrives
item.description: Macquarie Group Ltd. agreed to pay a small fine after admiting to failures in the way it promoted a savings account offer in its Australian retail bank, the division led at the time by now chief executive Greg Ward.

item.title: At China’s Big Import Fair, Sellers Try to Crack a Tough Market
item.description: There’s something for everyone at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai: American soybeans, German fountain pens, vitamins from Canada, camera lenses from Japan, blueberries from Zimbabwe.

item.title: House Nears Test Vote on Hegseth Impeachment
item.description: The House is set to vote Tuesday evening on whether to advance an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who cast the move as a politicized attack on US troops and lawful military operations ordered by President Donald Trump. Wendy Benjaminson, Bloomberg News National Security Team Leader discusses what's next for the Defense Secretary. (Source: Bloomberg)
